How AI drones are influencing the course of the Ukraine war
October 29, 2026 • Artificial intelligence is making drones faster and more capable. Russia and Ukraine both use AI-powered drones, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has warned that AI could lead decisions on the battlefield as soon as next year.

Why Ukraine and Russia agreed to a ceasefire in just one city
October 27, 2026 • Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a very limited ceasefire to help a Ukrainian city that’s been under Russian occupation for nearly five years. We hear about the horrific conditions residents have been living under in the city of Oleshky.

October 24, 2026 • Musk said Ukraine had been violating Starlink's terms by using it for military activity, as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said normal operating speeds have returned.
Ukrainian troops ride bikes under an anti-drone net in the frontline town of Druzhkivka, Ukraine, on Sept. 12. Both the Russian and Ukrainian forces have put up nets to guard against drones. October 18, 2026 • Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said he believes the U.S. government is behind his military's loss of normal access to the key satellite communications service used by the Ukrainian military.

October 17, 2026 • Zelenskyy described the move as unfortunate, adding it would encourage Russia to continue its assault. Trump told Congress that the pause was in the national interest but gave no further details.

A conversation with President Volodmyr Zelenskyy of Ukraine

October 8, 2026 • The South Korean announcement on Thursday came days after its President Lee Jae Myung threatened unspecified punitive steps if Ukraine refuses to apologize over the revelation.

Russia changes what it is attacking in Ukraine’s capital
October 5, 2026 • Russia's jet-powered drones are targeting bridges in the Ukrainian capital, an escalation after more than a month of day-and-night strikes that have left Kyiv feeling almost like a frontline city.

October 5, 2026 • The front line in the Russia-Ukraine war stretches more than 700 miles and has barely moved in four years. Yet straddling this line is the kill zone, dominated by constantly evolving drone technology.

September 20, 2026 • Moscow's mayor described the wave of drones as the "largest ever" attack on the Russian capital and said there had been damage to a Moscow oil refinery and a residential building.

A Russian election and a warning to Europe about Russian aggression

September 17, 2026 • Russia is believed to be holding thousands of Ukrainian soldiers and civilians as prisoners of war. In addition, Russia is tormenting the families of these prisoners by contacting them on social media and demanding favors. We hear from some of these family members.

Russia seizes Ukrainian POWs, then it demands favors from their relatives
September 16, 2026 • Russia is believed to be holding thousands of Ukrainian POWs. Russia is also tormenting the families of these prisoners by contacting their relatives on social media and demanding they help Russia.

Witkoff and Kushner call Kyiv talks 'substantive' after Moscow Putin meeting
September 6, 2026 • U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held meetings in Kyiv with Ukraine's President Zelenskyy on Sunday, a day after lengthy conversations with Russian President Putin in Moscow.

Russia’s increased attacks on Kyiv and its partnership with Iran
September 2, 2026 • Life has changed recently in the Ukrainian capital city of Kyiv. Residents there had gotten used to periodic Russian airstrikes happening maybe once or twice a week. But now the attacks are more constant using drones, ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, even hypersonic missiles - not only during the night, but now during the day. We hear from the mayor of Kyiv.

Russian strike near Kyiv kills 37, in one of the year's deadliest attacks
August 29, 2026 • The deadly strike comes amid 72 hours of near constant drone strikes across Ukraine, severely disrupting daily life.

U.K. will help Ukraine make long-range missiles by sharing classified tech information
August 25, 2026 • Burnham, who was in Kyiv for Ukraine's Independence Day, said defense firm MBDA will release details on U.K.-made parts for the SCALP missile to Ukraine to help the country assemble the weapons.

Ukraine launches one of its largest aerial attacks of the war, killing at least 6 people in Russia
August 16, 2026 • Ukraine launched hundreds of drones across Russia Sunday, killing at least six people in one of Kyiv's largest aerial attacks of the war.
Diners sit at an outdoor restaurant in Sevastopol, Crimea, on July 22. Ukrainian drone strikes are causing power outages, fuel shortages and cuts in cellphone service in the peninsula. By sky and sea, Ukraine's drone strikes challenge Russia's grip on Crimea
August 13, 2026 • Russia maintained an iron grip on Crimea since seizing it from Ukraine in 2014. Many Russian civilians go there to enjoy the beaches. But now Ukraine is hitting Crimea hard, upending daily life.

Ukraine mourns 'collector of souls' Oleksiy Yukov, killed recovering war dead
August 8, 2026 • Oleksiy Yukov spent two decades recovering the bodies of soldiers — including many Russians. He was killed during a recovery mission after stepping on a landmine.

Why Russia’s strikes on Ukraine are more intense; Germany’s song of the summer
August 4, 2026 • Ukraine’s defense forces have beaten back many types of Russian attacks during more than four years of war. But recently there has been a glaring weakness in their defenses: from Russian ballistic missiles. Those kinds of attacks are repelled by U.S.-made Patriot air defense missiles. Ukraine is desperately short of them and even the U.S. supplies of Patriot missiles are dwindling. We go to Kyiv to hear what the shortage means for Ukraine.

The soaring demand for Patriot missiles, from the Middle East to Ukraine
August 4, 2026 • The U.S. and its partners depend on Patriot interceptors to shoot down incoming ballistic missiles. But Russia and Iran are firing their weapons at rates far higher than Patriots can be produced.
